# Content review

Every factual claim in the Frequency Lab, for locator sign-off.

- **How to sign off:** add the claim to `content/review/signoffs.json` with the hash shown, your initials and the date. Or send the IDs and we'll add them.
- **Edited claims:** editing a claim changes its hash and puts it back in review.

**State-specific claims:** none so far. The lab teaches no state rules.

## Signal model calibrations

Teaching values from `src/signal/constants.ts`. `docs/SIGNAL_MODEL.md` explains how they combine and lists the eight resulting states.

| ID | Calibration | Hash | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model.block-length` | Block length: 140 ft. Long enough to see the signal fade in the 3D view, short enough to show street detail. | `5d6de62c12` | Not reviewed |
| `model.chart-length` | Chart length: 500 ft. Reach differences between frequencies show clearly over a few hundred feet. | `3d68075897` | Not reviewed |
| `model.water-main-crossing` | Water main crossing: 100 ft. Inside the block and well away from the hookup, so it reads as a separate feature. | `0939f470ae` | Not reviewed |
| `model.fade-on-the-coated-steel-main` | Fade on the coated steel main: 512 Hz: 0.93, 8 kHz: 0.72, 33 kHz: 0.4, 83 kHz: 0.15 (share left per 100 ft). Higher frequencies leak through the pipe coating into the soil more easily, so they fade sooner and don't travel as far. Compressed so the difference shows within one block: real lines fade far more gradually, in the same order. | `0531664ab2` | Not reviewed |
| `model.fade-on-the-tracer-wire` | Fade on the tracer wire: 512 Hz: 0.95, 8 kHz: 0.8, 33 kHz: 0.5, 83 kHz: 0.34 (share left per 100 ft). The same trend as the steel main, compressed the same way. A thin insulated wire leaks less than the big coated main at every frequency. | `ca6e8e853b` | Not reviewed |
| `model.bleed-over-onto-the-telecom-cable` | Bleed-over onto the telecom cable: 512 Hz: 0.02, 8 kHz: 0.06, 33 kHz: 0.15, 83 kHz: 0.32 (share of target current). Coupling onto a nearby metal line grows with frequency, so higher frequencies bleed over more. | `ee73b3a16d` | Not reviewed |
| `model.circuit-resistance-steel-main` | Circuit resistance, steel main: 512 Hz: 60, 8 kHz: 56, 33 kHz: 52, 83 kHz: 48 (Ω). A long, well-grounded metal main is a good circuit at every frequency. Higher frequencies find a little more path through the soil. | `81c441a0bd` | Not reviewed |
| `model.circuit-resistance-tracer-wire` | Circuit resistance, tracer wire: 512 Hz: 500, 8 kHz: 490, 33 kHz: 480, 83 kHz: 470 (Ω). A thin wire grounded at its far end makes a higher-resistance circuit than a big steel main, so less current flows. | `f4f0a1bc95` | Not reviewed |
| `model.transmitter-output` | Transmitter output: 50 V. An illustrative output that gives readings in a familiar range. | `c65cc44c24` | Not reviewed |
| `model.transmitter-internal-resistance` | Transmitter internal resistance: 50 Ω. Keeps the current on a good circuit in the hundreds of milliamps rather than unlimited. | `5e51402e08` | Not reviewed |
| `model.enough-signal-to-trace` | Enough signal to trace: 20 mA. An illustrative threshold. Real needs depend on depth, soil and the receiver. | `e8f94dca9f` | Not reviewed |
